title: Spider-Man 4 Dominates India Box Office, DC Holds Strong as Ohh My Dog Crashes to ₹20 Lakh
text:
MUMBAI, August 13, 2026
Spider-Man Brand New Day box office collection remained dominant on its second Wednesday as the Tom Holland-led superhero blockbuster added an estimated ₹6.45 crore net in India. The film has now reached approximately ₹438 crore net, while its India gross total is estimated at nearly ₹524 crore.
Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey also remained in theaters nearly four weeks after its release. Among the newer Indian films, DC: The Bloody Valentine maintained a respectable weekday performance, while Pankaj Tripathi’s Ohh My Dog slipped into the lakh range.
All figures are preliminary industry estimates. Final totals can vary because some trackers report net collections while others publish gross receipts.
Latest India Box Office Collection Film Wednesday estimate Reported running total Collection basis Spider-Man: Brand New Day ₹6.45 crore ₹438 crore India net DC: The Bloody Valentine About ₹5 crore ₹37.50 crore Estimated India net The Odyssey ₹1.71 crore ₹173.87 crore Reported India gross Ohh My Dog ₹20 lakh ₹3.95 crore India net estimate Spider-Man: Brand New Day Continues Record-Breaking Run Spider-Man: Brand New Day has continued its extraordinary performance at the Indian box office despite entering the final days of its second week.
The superhero film collected an estimated ₹6.45 crore net on Wednesday, its 14th day in theaters. That took its estimated India net collection to approximately ₹438 crore.
The movie reportedly earned about ₹334.75 crore net during its first week and added approximately ₹103.25 crore during the second-week period covered by the latest estimates.
Its gross collection, which includes taxes, is higher. Current estimates place the film’s India gross total at about ₹523.64 crore.
The film has also become the highest-grossing non-Indian release at the Indian box office, overtaking previous Hollywood record holders. Its success has been powered by premium-format screens, dubbed versions and strong demand in major metropolitan markets.
Although Wednesday’s collection was lower than Tuesday’s estimated ₹8.50 crore, the film maintained a clear lead over competing releases. Latest Spider-Man: Brand New Day collection estimates
Ohh My Dog Falls to ₹20 Lakh Pankaj Tripathi’s Ohh My Dog has struggled to maintain momentum after a modest opening weekend. The Hindi drama earned an estimated ₹20 lakh on Wednesday, taking its six-day India net collection to approximately ₹3.95 crore.
The film opened below ₹1 crore on August 7. It found limited growth over its opening weekend but suffered a sharp fall once the weekday period began.
Its performance has also been affected by intense competition from Spider-Man: Brand New Day , The Odyssey and the stronger-than-expected showing of DC: The Bloody Valentine .
With its daily earnings now measured in lakhs, the movie will need a substantial increase over the Independence Day weekend to remain competitive. However, new theatrical releases and reduced show allocations could make that recovery difficult.
DC: The Bloody Valentine Maintains Strong Weekday Business Tamil action-crime drama DC: The Bloody Valentine has performed considerably better than Ohh My Dog , even though both films opened on August 7.
The movie earned about ₹5 crore net on Wednesday, according to early estimates, taking its India net collection to approximately ₹37.50 crore. Other trackers using gross figures placed its six-day nationwide total above ₹43 crore.
The difference highlights the importance of distinguishing between net and gross collections. Net earnings exclude entertainment taxes, while gross totals include them.
Directed by Arun Matheswaran, the film marks filmmaker Lokesh Kanagaraj’s acting debut. Wamiqa Gabbi and Sanjana also play important roles, while Anirudh Ravichander has composed the music.
The film opened primarily in Tamil but also reached viewers through dubbed versions. Its strongest support has come from southern markets, including Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.
With the Independence Day holiday approaching, the film could benefit from higher theater attendance if it retains enough screens.
The Odyssey Remains Steady After Nearly Four Weeks Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey continued its durable theatrical run on Wednesday, adding an estimated ₹1.71 crore in India.
The epic has been playing for approximately 26 days and has accumulated a reported India gross collection of about ₹173.87 crore. Some trade databases place its running total slightly lower because of differences in language-wise reporting and the treatment of previews.
The film began its Indian run with approximately ₹17.40 crore net and ₹20.76 crore gross on its opening day. Premium formats, particularly IMAX screenings, have played a significant role in sustaining its performance.
Despite losing screens to Spider-Man: Brand New Day and newer Indian releases, The Odyssey has continued to attract audiences. Its longer theatrical run demonstrates the staying power of Nolan’s films in India, especially among premium-format viewers.
Which Film Is Leading the Box Office? There is a substantial gap between Spider-Man: Brand New Day and every other movie currently playing in Indian theaters.
At approximately ₹438 crore net and nearly ₹524 crore gross, the Marvel-Sony film is operating on a much larger commercial scale than the other releases.
Among the August 7 Indian films, DC: The Bloody Valentine is clearly ahead of Ohh My Dog . Meanwhile, The Odyssey remains a stable older release despite entering its fourth week.
The upcoming Independence Day holiday could lift overall theater attendance. However, screen allocation, ticket prices, regional demand and competition from fresh releases will determine how much each movie benefits.
Editorial note: Box-office figures are estimates compiled from trade tracking and theater reporting. Producers may announce different totals, particularly when comparing India net, India gross and worldwide gross collections.
summary: Spider-Man Brand New Day box office collection remained dominant on its second Wednesday as the Tom Holland-led superhero blockbuster added an estimated ₹6.45 crore net in India. Among the newer Indian films, DC: The Bloody Valentine maintained a respectable weekday performance, while Pankaj Tripathi’s Ohh My Dog slipped into the lakh range. Although Wednesday’s collection was lower than Tuesday’s estimated ₹8.50 crore, the film maintained a clear lead over competing releases. The Hindi drama earned an estimated ₹20 lakh on Wednesday, taking its six-day India net collection to approximately ₹3.95 crore.
